General notes: - Assistant systems support the driver but do not replace attention or responsibility.
- The driver must always maintain control of the vehicle.
- Each system has limitations depending on traffic, weather, and road conditions.
Drive assist sensors and cameras: - Sensors and cameras detect surroundings for assistant functions.
- Keep sensors and lenses clean and unobstructed.
- Extreme weather may affect sensor performance.
- Sensors are located in the front, rear, and exterior mirrors.
Cruise control system: - Maintains a set speed without pressing the accelerator.
- Can be paused and resumed at any time.
- Automatically deactivates when braking or clutching.
Speed limiter: - Prevents the vehicle from exceeding a preset speed.
- The driver can override the limit by pressing the accelerator firmly.
- System alerts when the limit is approached.
- Adjustable via the steering controls or infotainment.
Speed limiter with proactive speed adjus: - Adjusts speed based on detected speed limits.
- Uses navigation and camera data for predictions.
- Can be combined with cruise control for smooth driving.
- The driver can override at any time.
Eco Assistance: - Provides driving tips to reduce energy consumption.
- Suggests when to lift off the accelerator.
ACC - Adaptive Cruise Control: - Maintains set speed and safe distance from the vehicle in front.
- Automatically accelerates and brakes within limits.
- Distance and dynamics adjustable via infotainment.
- Alerts if driver intervention is required.
Predictive speed adjustment: - Adjusts speed in anticipation of curves, junctions, and limits.
- Uses map data and sensors to prepare for changes.
- Can be enabled or disabled in settings.
Emergency brake assistance system (Front: - Warns of possible collisions with vehicles or pedestrians.
- Initiates automatic braking if the driver doesn’t react.
- May apply full braking force in critical situations.
Lane Assist system: - Detects lane markings and keeps the vehicle centered.
- Provides corrective steering if lane is unintentionally left.
- Active above a certain speed threshold.
- Requires hands on the wheel; may deactivate otherwise.
Travel Assist: - Combines Lane Assist and Adaptive Cruise Control.
- Maintains speed, distance, and keeps the vehicle in lane.
- Requires driver supervision and hands on the wheel.
- Visual signals in Digital Cockpit show active status.
Emergency Assist: - Detects driver inactivity and attempts to reactivate.
- Slows the vehicle to a stop if the driver is unresponsive.
- Activates hazard lights and calls emergency services (if equipped).
Lane departure warning (Side Assist): - Monitors blind spots and alerts when vehicles are nearby.
- Provides visual signals in mirrors or cockpit.
- May intervene to prevent unsafe lane changes.
- Works together with Rear Traffic Alert during reversing.
